analysis.title: Global: GS Economic Indicators Update: Wage Growth Slows Further in the US
key_insights: GS US Wage Tracker slowed to 3.0% year-over-year in Q3. GS estimates this pace is consistent with below-target inflation.
The GS Global ex Russia FCI tightened by 4.0bps last week, primarily on long rates and equities.

GS GDP forecast revisions over the past 60 days were positive across Asia. Taiwan's 2026 forecast rose 2pp over 60 days and 1.4pp over the past week. Taiwan's 2027 forecast rose 3.7pp over 60 days and 3pp over the past week.
The preliminary September global CAI is +3.3% (3-month average, annualized) against spot +3.2%. GS describes the global CAI as remaining notably above its 2.7% potential.
The preliminary September US CAI is +3.0% on a 3-month average with a weekly change of -0.4. Spot is +3.6%. 92% of US data has been released.
Developed markets CAI is +2.3% (3-month average) against spot +2.6%. Emerging markets CAI is +4.7% (3-month average) against spot +4.1%, with a weekly change of +0.2.
Within the Euro Area (54% of data released), the September CAI is +1.4% on a 3-month average with spot at +1.1%. Spain is +2.8%, Germany +0.4%, France +0.9% and Italy +0.9% on a 3-month average.
Russia's preliminary September CAI rose 0.7pp on the week to +1.7%. Spain's fell 0.7pp to +2.8%.
Within EM, India's CAI is +7.4% and China's is +5.4% on a 3-month average. Brazil is -0.6% and South Africa +0.5%.
GS short-run utilization scores (percent of potential) show the US at -1.8, UK at -0.7, Japan at -1.1 and Canada at -1.4. Italy (+4.8) and Spain (+5.3) are the tightest in Europe.
The UK has the weakest reading in the GS MAP Surprise Index at -3.6. The index is the 21-day moving average of daily economic data surprises against consensus.

The report includes updates on FCI impulses, fiscal impulses, trimmed core inflation, inflation surprise indices, jobs-workers gaps, wage survey leading indicators, and GS inflation and GDP forecast changes versus other forecasters. The text carries no numeric detail for these exhibits.
